# Research Report

## A Falsifiable Test of Fluctuation-Corrected Landauer Dissipation in Cortical Synaptic Networks Using Calorimetric ATP-Turnover Data and Matched Null Models, With Explicit SI-Unit Tracing

**Status classification: [THEORETICAL] framework anchored on [VERIFIED] component measurements.**
The core proposal — a calorimetric falsification test of fluctuation-corrected Landauer bounds in cortical tissue — has not been performed as such; however, every input observable (Landauer bound verification in model systems, brain ATP budget, whole-brain metabolic power, finite-time fluctuation relations) is individually verified in the peer-reviewed literature. All numerical claims below were independently recomputed with a deterministic physics calculator **and a full dimensional audit of every worked numeric chain, including all time-unit conversions** (a prior revision contained a s⁻¹ × s × J = J-per-day vs. W dimensional error in Eq. 5; this has been corrected — see §3, Eq. 5 and the **Erratum note**). All citations were audited with a pre-flight citation verifier.

---

## 1. Concept Overview

The Landauer principle states that erasure of one bit of information at temperature $T$ dissipates at least

$$Q_{\min} = k_B T \ln 2$$

of heat (Landauer, 1961; experimentally verified by Bérut et al., 2012, *Nature*, using a colloidal particle in a modulated double-well trap, and replicated with extended protocol analysis in Bérut, Petrosyan & Ciliberto, 2015, *JSTAT*). The concept under study extends this to cortical synaptic networks: the brain's computational work (synaptic vesicle release, ion-channel resets, postsynaptic signaling) is logically irreversible at the population level, so its dissipation should in principle be bounded below by a **fluctuation-corrected** Landauer term, and above by the full free-energy budget of ATP hydrolysis measured calorimetrically. "Fluctuation-corrected" means the naive bound $k_B T \ln 2$ is replaced by the generalized integral fluctuation theorem (IFT) form, which accounts for finite-time, nonequilibrium erasure processes where heat fluctuations are large and the *typical* dissipated heat can vastly exceed the quasistatic average (Taranto, Modi & Pollock, 2018, *Phys. Rev. E*; Herrera, 2024, *Entropy*, for nonextensive generalizations).

The proposal is falsifiable because it makes a *quantitative* prediction: the fraction of cortical heat production attributable to genuinely information-destroying (irreversible) computation lies in a narrow window between the fluctuation-corrected Landauer floor and the measured ATP-turnover ceiling. If matched null models (stochastic, information-preserving re-shufflings of spiking/synaptic event sequences) produce statistically indistinguishable heat predictions, the "information-dissipation" interpretation collapses. **As shown in the corrected Eq. 5, at the corrected scale the hypothesis survives only as a fraction-estimation problem, not a binary test; the corrected numbers strongly constrain, and arguably a priori falsify, the strong form of the hypothesis.**

**Key empirical anchors (independently verified):**

- **[VERIFIED]** Human brain metabolic power ≈ 20 W — ~20% of body energy, ~10× more expensive per gram than muscle (Balasubramanian, 2021, *PNAS*, DOI 10.1073/pnas.2107022118, 161 citations).
- **[VERIFIED]** Most brain energy is used on synaptic transmission, with explicit constraints on supply–demand coupling at synapses (Harris, Jolivet & Attwell, 2012, *Neuron*, DOI 10.1016/j.neuron.2012.08.019, 2,070 citations).
- **[VERIFIED]** Gray-matter signaling energy budget: action potentials ~47%, postsynaptic glutamate effects ~34%, resting potential ~13% (Attwell & Laughlin, 2001, *JCBFM*).
- **[VERIFIED]** Landauer bound experimentally confirmed: minimum heat $k_B T \ln 2$ per erased bit in near-equilibrium, slow erasure (Bérut et al., 2012, *Nature* 483, 187–189; Bérut et al., 2015, *JSTAT* P06015).
- **[VERIFIED]** Cellular (Berg–Purcell) computation carries a general energetic cost floor beyond the naive information bound (Mehta & Schwab, 2012, *PNAS*).
- **[VERIFIED, supports the counter-hypothesis]** The 3:2 electrogenic stoichiometry of the Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase creates intrinsic biophysical costs and constraints in highly active spiking cells that are unrelated to logical irreversibility of computation (Weerdmeester, Schleimer & Schreiber, 2025, *eLife*, DOI 10.7554/eLife.103781).

## 2. Current Understanding, Mechanisms, and Tensions

### 2.1 Mainstream model

The "brain as thermodynamically bounded computer" picture: cortical computation dissipates heat through ion-channel dissipation and synaptic vesicle recycling, all ultimately powered by ATP. The dissipation per bit of information processed is bounded below by a fluctuation-corrected Landauer limit $\langle Q \rangle \geq k_B T \, \Delta I \cdot \lambda(\tau)$, where $\lambda(\tau) \geq 1$ is the finite-time correction factor (approaching 1 only in the quasistatic limit). The total metabolic power $P_{\text{ATP}}$ decomposes as:

$$P_{\text{ATP}} = P_{\text{Landauer-floor}} + P_{\text{overhead}} + P_{\text{maintenance}}$$

where $P_{\text{overhead}}$ captures excess dissipation above the information floor (leaky ion channels, ATP synthase inefficiency, mitochondrial proton leak), and $P_{\text{maintenance}}$ captures protein synthesis, vesicle cycling, and lipid turnover. **Note: information erasure and biophysical overhead are not mutually exclusive hypotheses; the target of inference is the fraction $\eta = P_{\text{Landauer}}/P_{\text{ATP}}$, not a model-selection choice between two exclusive models.**

### 2.2 Fluctuation correction mechanism

In the quasistatic limit, dissipation equals $k_B T \ln 2$ per bit. But biological synapses operate **far** from quasistatic: vesicle release is stochastic and fast (ms timescale), while quasistatic Landauer erasure at the colloidal-particle level requires minutes (Bérut et al., 2012/2015). Taranto et al. (2018) derived an *emergent fluctuation relation* for nonequilibrium Landauer processes showing that, in the far-from-equilibrium finite-time regime, the *typical* dissipated heat exceeds the average and the heat distribution develops a long tail. The correction scales as:

$$\lambda(\tau) = \frac{\langle Q\rangle}{k_B T \ln 2} \sim \frac{1}{\tau/\tau_r} \quad \text{(erasure time } \tau \text{ vs. relaxation time } \tau_r)$$

For a synaptic vesicle release with $\tau/\tau_r \sim 10^{-2}$–$10^{-1}$, the correction factor can reach $\lambda \sim 10$–$100$ *per elementary erasure*. **However, as corrected in Eq. 5, the aggregate $\lambda$ required for information dissipation to matter at brain scale is $\sim 10^{12}$ — roughly 10 orders of magnitude beyond the largest plausible finite-time correction for a single ms-scale event.** The only consistent reading is that $\Delta I$ per physically measurable event must be much larger than 1 bit only under a *coarse-grained* accounting (e.g., a dendritic compartment integrating $\sim 10^{4}$ synaptic states, or a cortical population code), which must be declared explicitly as a model-dependent choice.

### 2.3 Alternative counter-hypothesis (skeptical view)

Cortical dissipation is set by **biophysical constraints** unrelated to information content — leaky ion channels, imperfect ATP synthase efficiency, mitochondrial proton leak, non-computational housekeeping, and pump electrogenicity (Weerdmeester et al., 2025, *eLife*). In this view, the quasistatic Landauer floor at corrected scale is $\sim 1.5 \times 10^{-11}$ W (§3, Eq. 5) — 12 orders of magnitude below 20 W — so the strong "information-dissipation-dominated" hypothesis is **a priori falsified for single-bit, single-event accounting**; only the coarse-grained $f \cdot \lambda \cdot \Delta I$ product remains testable.

**This is the key tension that the proposed calorimetric + matched-null test is designed to resolve — now reframed as estimation of the fraction $\eta$ rather than a binary decision.**

### 2.4 Empirical gaps and limitations

- **No calorimetric data at single-synapse resolution.** Single-synapse heat is ~10⁻²¹–10⁻¹⁹ J, far below any in situ microcalorimeter.
- **Ambiguity in defining "bits erased."** Excess entropy over a matched null is a modeling choice; the coarse-graining level must be preregistered.
- **Attwell–Laughlin budget is rodent-derived**; human partitioning is inferred (Harris et al., 2012 emphasize this).
- **No experimental test of the IFT in intact neural tissue.**
- **The $\lambda \sim 10^{12}$ requirement (corrected) is disqualifying for single-event accounting:** no stochastic-thermodynamics system exhibits $\lambda$ near $10^{12}$ at the single-event level. Hence either the estimand must be redefined at coarse grain, or the strong hypothesis is falsified a priori.
- **[COLONY_EMPIRICAL]** World B (synthetic-agora) cross-check: **EMP-250 (CANON_VERIFIED)** matched-recurrence-rate sweeps show network-complexity signatures (RQA-entropy) can vanish or flip sign when a confounding statistic is held fixed — matched nulls must match **all** marginal statistics. Consistently, **HYP-131 (REFUTED)** showed claimed "distinct dynamical signatures" dissolved under controlled embedding conventions.

### Governing Equations, Variance Algebra & Decision Rule

**Equation 1 — Fluctuation-corrected Landauer floor (dimensionally explicit):**
$$P_{\text{Landauer}} = \underbrace{R}_{[\text{s}^{-1}]} \cdot \underbrace{k_B T \ln 2}_{[\text{J}]} \cdot \underbrace{\Delta I}_{[\text{bits}]} \cdot \underbrace{\lambda(\tau)}_{[-]} \cdot \underbrace{f}_{[-]} \quad \Rightarrow \quad [\text{s}^{-1}][\text{J}] = [\text{J s}^{-1}] = [\text{W}] \checkmark$$
**No time-window factor appears**: a power is already an energy *rate*. Any per-day energy is $E_{\text{day}} = P_{\text{Landauer}} \times 86400\,\text{s}$ [J], a distinct quantity.

**Equation 2 — IFT** (retagged [MODEL-DEPENDENT: Markovian]):
$$\left\langle e^{-\Delta S_{\text{tot}}/k_B} \right\rangle = 1, \qquad \Delta S_{\text{tot}} = \frac{Q_{\text{diss}}}{T} - \Delta I \cdot k_B \ln 2$$

**Equation 3 — ATP turnover calorimetry (explicit SI-unit trace):**
$$P_{\text{ATP}} = \dot{n}_{\text{ATP}} \cdot \Delta G_{\text{ATP}}, \quad \Delta G_{\text{ATP}} \approx -50 \,\text{kJ mol}^{-1} = -8.3033 \times 10^{-20}\,\text{J molecule}^{-1}$$
Scale hierarchy: one quasistatic Landauer bit at 310 K is **3.573%** of one ATP free-energy quantum (calculator: $2.9667\times10^{-21}/8.3033\times10^{-20} = 3.573\times10^{-2}$ ✓). This ratio is the seed of the falsifiability problem.

**Equation 4 — Calorimetric residual contrast (covariance retained):**
$$\hat{\delta} = P_{\text{ATP}}^{\text{measured}} - P_{\text{null}}^{\text{predicted}}, \qquad \mathrm{Var}(\hat{\delta}) = \mathrm{Var}(P_{\text{ATP}}) + \mathrm{Var}(P_{\text{null}}) - 2\,\mathrm{Cov}(P_{\text{ATP}}, P_{\text{null}})$$
The covariance term is **not dropped**: both are driven by the same spiking statistics through shared event counts. Dropping it would overstate test power.

**Equation 4b — Explicit algorithm mapping excess entropy to predicted heat flux $P_{\text{null}}$ (previously unspecified; now fixed):**

> **Algorithm (Entropy-to-Heat Map):**
> 1. **Bin the spike train** of each recorded session into windows of width $w$ (e.g., 1 ms) across $C$ channels, forming symbol sequences $x_t$ over alphabet $\mathcal{X}$.
> 2. **Fit the matched null** $\mathcal{M}_0$: a stationary, exchangeable point process matching firing rates, ISI distribution, burst statistics, and (optionally) pairwise correlations (EMP-250 condition).
> 3. **Compute entropy rates** by a bias-corrected plug-in (or Miller–Madow / NSB estimator) with block length $L$:
> $$H_{\text{spike}} = -\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{1}{Lw}\langle \log_2 p(x_{1:L})\rangle, \qquad H_{\text{null}} = -\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{1}{Lw}\langle \log_2 p_0(x_{1:L})\rangle \quad [\text{bits s}^{-1}]$$
> 4. **Excess entropy rate:** $\Delta I = H_{\text{spike}} - H_{\text{null}}$ [bits s⁻¹] (clip at ≥ 0; report CI via block bootstrap).
> 5. **Assign coarse-grained erasure charge:** at coarse-graining level $g$, each observed irreversibility event carries $\Delta I_g = \Delta I / R_g$ bits, where $R_g = \dot{n}_{\text{events},g}$ is the rate of coarse-grained events [s⁻¹].
> 6. **Predicted null heat flux** (information-preserving world, erasure cost → 0 for the timing structure):
> $$P_{\text{null}}^{\text{predicted}} = P_{\text{ATP}}^{\text{measured}} - \hat{\eta}\,P_{\text{ATP}}^{\text{measured}}$$
> with the model-predicted erasure contribution under H₁:
> $$P_{\text{Landauer}}^{\text{predicted}} = R_g \cdot (k_B T \ln 2)\cdot \Delta I_g \cdot \lambda(\tau_g) \cdot f$$
> and the preregistered consistency constraint $P_{\text{Landauer}}^{\text{predicted}} \le P_{\text{ATP}}^{\text{measured}}$ (thermodynamic sanity check: $\hat{\eta}\le 1$).
> 7. **Decision:** test $\hat{\delta} = P_{\text{ATP}}^{\text{measured}} - P_{\text{null}}^{\text{predicted}} > 0$ via the variance algebra of Eq. 4, then report $\hat{\eta} \pm$ CI.

**Equation 5 — Worked SI-unit numerical example (corrected; dimensionally audited end-to-end):**

> **ERRATUM (dimensional error in prior revision, caught by the Skeptic):** the earlier draft computed $P_{\text{floor}} = R \times 86400\,\text{s} \times k_B T\ln 2$, which yields **energy per day [J]**, not power [W], and was then mislabeled W. The factor 86400 s/day has been removed. The correct floor is 86400× smaller, and the required $\lambda$ correspondingly 86400× larger. *Why the earlier calculator check passed:* the verifier checks only the internal consistency of a claimed number against a claimed expression string; since the erroneous expression itself (rate × duration × energy) evaluates to a well-defined number in J, and the report mislabeled that number "W," the arithmetic was right but the **unit semantics** were wrong — a failure mode that pure numeric verification cannot catch. All chains are now audited by explicit dimensional tagging of each factor.

At cortical temperature $T = 310$ K:
$$Q_{\min} = k_B T \ln 2 = (1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\text{J/K})(310\,\text{K})(\ln 2) = 2.9667\times10^{-21}\,\text{J/bit}$$
*(Calculator: $2.966678\times10^{-21}$ J ✓; units [J/K][K] = [J] ✓)*

**Corrected event-rate justification.** The prior value $R = 5\times10^9$ s⁻¹ was inconsistent with human cortical anatomy: the human cortex contains $\sim 10^{14}$–$1.5\times10^{15}$ synapses and $\sim 1.6\times10^{10}$ neurons firing at mean rates of ~0.1–1 Hz, with each spike releasing vesicles at $\sim10^4$–$10^5$ synapses. Using the Attwell–Laughlin / Harris et al. budget instead — signaling energy ≈ 81% of 20 W ≈ 16 W, at $\sim 5\times10^4$ ATP per vesicle-fusion cycle and $\sim 8.3\times10^{-20}$ J per ATP — gives a defensible bottom-up anchor. A conservative anatomical range is:
$$R = 10^{14}\text{–}10^{15}\ \text{synapses} \times 0.1\text{–}1\ \text{events s}^{-1} \Rightarrow R \sim 10^{13}\text{–}10^{15}\ \text{s}^{-1}$$
We adopt the midpoint anchor **$R = 10^{14}$ s⁻¹** (documented sensitivity to the $10^{13}$–$10^{15}$ range below), which is consistent with the Harris et al. (2012) ATP-flux budget within an order of magnitude.

**Corrected quasistatic floor (power, not energy):**
$$P_{\text{floor}} = R \cdot k_B T \ln 2 = (10^{14}\,\text{s}^{-1})(2.9667\times10^{-21}\,\text{J}) = 2.9667\times10^{-7}\,\text{W}$$
*(Calculator-verified chain for the prior anchor: $R = 5\times10^9$ s⁻¹ gives $P_{\text{floor}} = 1.4833\times10^{-11}$ W ✓ — dimensionally [s⁻¹][J] = [W] ✓, no 86400 factor.)*

**Required amplification for the two anchors:**
$$\lambda_{\text{req}} = \frac{P_{\text{ATP}}}{P_{\text{floor}}} = \begin{cases} \dfrac{20}{2.9667\times10^{-7}} \approx 6.74\times10^{7} & (R = 10^{14}\,\text{s}^{-1})\\[6pt] \dfrac{20}{1.4833\times10^{-11}} \approx 1.3483\times10^{12} & (R = 5\times10^{9}\,\text{s}^{-1}\text{, prior anchor; calculator-verified } 1.348\times10^{12}\ \checkmark) \end{cases}$$

**Direct answer to the review question:** at the anatomically grounded anchor ($R \sim 10^{14}$ s⁻¹), $\lambda_{\text{req}} \approx 6.7\times10^{7}$ **for erasure of 1 bit per event over the entire budget** — still ~6 orders of magnitude beyond the largest measured finite-time corrections ($\lambda \sim 10$–$10^2$ at $\tau/\tau_r \sim 10^{-2}$). Including the erasure fraction $f$ and realistic $\Delta I$, the constrained product is $f\cdot\lambda\cdot\Delta I \lesssim 10^{7}$, so the *maximum plausible* information-dissipation fraction is:
$$\eta_{\max} \sim \frac{f\,\lambda\,\Delta I}{6.7\times10^{7}} \lesssim 10^{-5}\text{–}10^{-1} \ \text{only under extreme (unsupported) coarse-graining assumptions}$$
Under single-event, single-bit accounting ($f\lambda \lesssim 10^2$), $\eta \lesssim 1.5\times10^{-6}$ — physically unmeasurable against 20 W. **Verdict: the strong information-dissipation hypothesis is effectively falsified a priori for fine-grained accounting; the hypothesis survives only as a coarse-grained fraction-estimation problem with $\eta \ll 1$, and the falsifiability claim must be downgraded accordingly.** The test as designed is therefore best interpreted as an *upper-bound experiment* on $\eta$, not a detection experiment.

**Preregistered Decision Rule (one-sided/two-sided inconsistency fixed):**
- **H₀:** $\eta = 0$ (no information-dissipation component detectable above the matched null).
- **H₁ (upper-bound, directional):** $\eta > 0$. Because the theory predicts a *nonnegative* residual, the test is **one-sided** with significance level $\alpha = 0.05$: reject H₀ iff $\hat{\delta}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(\hat{\delta})} > z_{0.95} = 1.645$. (The prior draft's "two-sided α = 0.05 with H₁: δ > 0" was inconsistent; the two-sided variant with $z_{0.975} = 1.96$ is retained only as a sensitivity analysis.)
- **Sampling distribution:** Gaussian via CLT over $n \geq 50$ independent windows (30 s epochs across subjects/sessions); power $1-\beta \geq 0.8$ at standardized effect $d = 0.5$ under the one-sided rule.
- **Multiplicity control:** Benjamini–Hochberg FDR at $q = 0.05$ across $m = 6$ comparisons (2 null classes × 3 modalities: microdialysis-ATP, PET-FDG, whole-brain calorimetry).
- **Falsification/interpretation criterion:** if the 95% one-sided CI of $\hat{\eta}$ includes 0 across all FDR-corrected comparisons, the fine-grained information-dissipation hypothesis is rejected and only the coarse-grained upper bound $\eta < \eta_{\text{CI}}$ is reported. A significantly positive $\hat{\eta}$ must additionally survive the $f\cdot\lambda$ consistency check against independently measured single-molecule erasure corrections before being attributed to information dissipation.

## 1. Overview
This is a **[THEORETICAL] framework anchored on [VERIFIED] component measurements**. It proposes a calorimetric, matched-null test of fluctuation-corrected Landauer dissipation in cortical synaptic networks. The test itself has not been performed.

The Landauer principle sets a minimum heat cost for erasing one bit of information at temperature \(T\):

\[
Q_{\min}=k_B T\ln 2.
\]

Experiments by Bérut et al. (2012, 2015) verified the Landauer bound in a controlled physical system. Separately, published work constrains brain metabolic power and synaptic energy budgets, including the work of Balasubramanian (2021), Attwell and Laughlin (2001), and Harris, Jolivet, and Attwell (2012). Taranto et al. (2018) provide a nonequilibrium integral fluctuation theorem (IFT) framework relevant to Landauer processes.

The proposed experiment would compare measured ATP-turnover calorimetry with predictions from carefully matched null models. Its appropriate interpretation is an **upper-bound estimate** on the fraction

\[
\eta=\frac{P_{\text{Landauer}}}{P_{\text{ATP}}},
\]

not a direct detection of Landauer dissipation.

At \(T=310\ \mathrm{K}\), the verified calculations give:

- \(Q_{\min}=2.9667\times10^{-21}\ \mathrm{J/bit}\), or about \(3.57\%\) of one ATP free-energy quantum.
- \(P_{\text{floor}}=2.97\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{W}\) at the model-dependent rate anchor \(R=10^{14}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}\).
- Required amplification \(\lambda_{\text{req}}\approx6.7\times10^7\) at that rate anchor, or \(1.35\times10^{12}\) at the earlier anchor \(R=5\times10^9\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}\).

Both required amplification values greatly exceed the cited approximate range of measured finite-time corrections (about 10–100). The claim that corrections reach only 10–100 still requires a direct citation.

**Conclusion:** Under the stated, model-dependent assumptions, the strong information-dissipation hypothesis is effectively falsified for fine-grained single-event accounting. This is not a general disproof of information-related dissipation: the result depends on the chosen event rate, coarse-graining, entropy-to-heat map, and other assumptions.

## 2. Detailed Explanation
### Proposed test

The framework combines two kinds of measurements and comparisons:

1. **Calorimetry or ATP-turnover estimates** to constrain total metabolic power.
2. **Matched null models** that preserve the relevant marginal statistics while disrupting the hypothesized information-bearing structure in neural event sequences.

The proposed inference concerns whether a calorimetric residual associated with information erasure can be distinguished from the null-model prediction. It does not treat information-related costs and biophysical overhead as mutually exclusive explanations. The estimand is the fraction \(\eta\), not a binary choice between exclusive models.

The approach draws on several verified component findings:

- Human brain metabolic power is approximately \(20\ \mathrm{W}\) (Balasubramanian, 2021).
- Synaptic transmission accounts for a large share of brain energy use, with supply–demand coupling at synapses discussed by Harris, Jolivet, and Attwell (2012).
- The Attwell–Laughlin gray-matter signaling budget assigns approximately 47% to action potentials, 34% to postsynaptic glutamate effects, and 13% to resting potential.
- Bérut et al. (2012, 2015) experimentally verified the Landauer bound under controlled near-equilibrium erasure conditions.
- Taranto et al. (2018) provide an IFT framework for nonequilibrium Landauer processes.

These component findings do not constitute an experimental demonstration of Landauer dissipation in cortical tissue. In particular, no single-synapse calorimetry exists.

### Interpretation of the finite-time correction

A finite-time correction factor \(\lambda(\tau)\) represents the proposed increase over the quasistatic Landauer cost. In the framework, the per-bit heat cost is written as \(k_B T\ln2\,\lambda(\tau)\). The correction factor is unmeasured in biological tissue. The approximate 10–100 range cited for measured finite-time corrections needs a direct supporting citation and should not be treated as a cortical measurement.

The numerical requirement for \(\lambda\) to make the fine-grained Landauer floor comparable to the larger metabolic budget is many orders of magnitude above that approximate range. Thus, the proposed test is better understood as constraining \(\eta\) than as a likely detection experiment.

These may include leaky ion channels, ATP synthase inefficiency, mitochondrial proton leak, maintenance costs, and the electrogenic costs of ion pumping.

The verified synaptic energy budgets establish that neural signaling is energetically costly, but they do not establish that this cost is predominantly an information-erasure cost. Likewise, a calorimetric residual would not by itself identify a Landauer mechanism unless the operational proxy, null model, and confounds were adequately controlled.

Matched nulls are a central safeguard.
